correctness.rationale: The derivative weights are derived from Lagrange interpolation. Expressing monotone samples by nonnegative increments turns the minimization into a cumulative-tail problem. Alternating decreasing magnitudes identify the second tail as the sharp minimum. A beta-integral converts the full positive-side coefficient sum to \(H_{2m}-H_m\), giving the exact defect. Rational replay verifies polynomial exactness, tail signs, extremizers, and harmonic identities for \(1\le m\le40\).

value.rationale: The monotone-sample cone is a natural shape constraint, and centered finite differences are ubiquitous. The theorem completely quantifies their sign-reversal defect across every formal order, shows the defect worsens monotonically, and gives exact extremal data and a nonzero limiting fraction. This is a structural benchmark rather than a single low-order counterexample.
